A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text and complete appendices. Text comparison and visual inspection support matching the equations, figures, tables, and relocated material.

before.justification: v2 Appendix C reports original numerical experiments on synthetic k-PARITY, including RL and SFT gradient visualizations in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v3 Appendix D retains those original k-PARITY experiments and their gradient visualizations in Figures 5–6.

M1.justification: The masked one-layer transformer, activations, RL reward, SFT objectives, and update procedures are retained. Calling the process reward 'verifiable' clarifies its existing definition; the serial-CoT and general-loss extensions already appeared in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions experimentally study synthetic k-PARITY with d = 20 and k = 16. AND and OR remain theoretical examples; no evaluated dataset, task, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The numerical study retains the same comparison between process-reward RL and SFT without teacher forcing. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The experimental description is identical: 50,000 uniformly sampled inputs, a random relevant-bit subset, four reasoning steps, all-ones initialization, and the same gradient-sign computations.

E4.justification: Figures 5–6 retain the same gradient-separation and successive-update analyses. No new ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study appears; the additional explanatory schematic presents existing findings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 5–6 contain identical experimental heatmaps and retain the findings of simultaneous RL learning and successive SFT-step learning. No numerical values, result entries, or qualitative outcomes change.

T1.justification: The main theorems, propositions, assumptions, and appendix derivations are retained, including the serial-CoT extension. Appendix renumbering and local changes to ground-truth notation in old Appendix G/new Appendix H do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly qualifies stepwise SFT learning as occurring without teacher forcing, and the abstract and discussion foreground dependence on supervision. This refines the headline contrast while retaining the same learnability contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 develops the interpretation through informative feedback on training states and newly situates SFT without teacher forcing within broader training on self-generated trajectories. The limitations in new Appendix A largely preserve v2's existing discussion.

D1.justification: The disclosed initialization, synthetic-data construction, model specification, and training procedures remain unchanged. v3 adds no implementation resources, hyperparameters, compute details, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al. (2026) on implicit curriculum in RLVR and a short discussion in Appendix C. Existing comparisons, including the detailed positioning against Kim and Suzuki (2025), are retained across relocation.

P1.justification: The abstract, selected introduction passages, and discussion are rewritten. Limitations move to Appendix A, and the detailed novelty comparison moves into related work; most technical prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn as a full-width schematic showing trajectories, rewards, and supervision, with an expanded caption. Figures 5–6 are placed together on page 16; their contents and the other figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised abstract and expanded Figure 1 make the existing supervision and teacher-forcing qualifications easier to understand, improving exposition without changing the proofs or empirical evidence. Figure 1 retains a stale Appendix A/Q4 reference, but this small navigation defect does not outweigh the clearer explanation.
